pinyin: bǎo shí zhōng rì, wú suǒ yòng xīn
literal: full · eat · whole · day, no · place · use · mind
natural: Eating one's fill all day and putting one's mind to nothing

meaning.en: Describes someone idle who lives aimlessly; a criticism of laziness.
meaning.zh: 整天吃饱了饭，什么事也不用心，形容无所事事、游手好闲。

examples.zh: 他毕业后“饱食终日，无所用心”，一事无成。
examples.en: After graduating he idled about with no purpose and achieved nothing.

examples.zh: 孔子批评“饱食终日，无所用心”的人很难有出息。
examples.en: Confucius criticised idlers as unlikely to amount to anything.

story.en: Confucius says: 'To eat your fill all day and put your mind to nothing is hard indeed! Are there not games like chess? Even playing them is better than doing nothing.'
story.zh: 孔子说：“饱食终日，无所用心，难矣哉！不有博弈者乎？为之犹贤乎已。”

usage.en: A quotation from the classics; formal, used to support an argument or give advice.
usage.zh: 经典引文，书面语，常用来论证或劝勉。

text: 运筹帷幄之中，决胜千里之外
pinyin: yùn chóu wéi wò zhī zhōng, jué shèng qiān lǐ zhī wài
variants: 运筹策帷帐之中，决胜于千里之外
literal: plan · tent · curtains · of · within, decide · victory · thousand · li · of · outside
natural: Plan strategy within the command tent and decide victory a thousand li away

meaning.en: A skilled strategist can direct a distant campaign from behind the lines.
meaning.zh: 在帐幕中谋划策略，就能决定千里之外战场的胜负，形容善于指挥、深谋远虑。

examples.zh: 总指挥在指挥部里“运筹帷幄之中，决胜千里之外”。
examples.en: The commander directed the operation from the control room.

examples.zh: 项目经理善于“运筹帷幄之中，决胜千里之外”，团队按他的计划稳步推进。
examples.en: The project manager plans carefully and the team moves steadily along his plan.

story.en: Liu Bang, the first Han emperor, credited his victory to three men: 'in planning strategy in the command tent and winning victories a thousand li away I am not equal to Zhang Liang'. The original reads 夫运筹策帷帐之中，决胜于千里之外.
story.zh: 刘邦总结得天下之因，称“夫运筹策帷帐之中，决胜于千里之外，吾不如子房”。

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

pinyin: yī zé yǐ xǐ, yī zé yǐ yōu
literal: one · side · be glad, one · side · be anxious
natural: On the one hand it brings joy, on the other worry

meaning.en: Mixed feelings: pleased at one aspect and anxious about another; originally about a parent's age.
meaning.zh: 既高兴又担忧；原指为父母的高寿而喜、又为其年迈而忧。

examples.zh: 孩子考上了外地大学，妈妈“一则以喜，一则以忧”。
examples.en: Her child got into a university in another city and the mother felt both glad and worried.

examples.zh: 得知父亲八十大寿，他“一则以喜，一则以忧”。
examples.en: On his father's eightieth birthday he felt joy tinged with worry.

story.en: Confucius said: 'A child must know the age of his parents: on the one hand it is a joy, on the other a cause for worry.'
story.zh: 孔子说：“父母之年，不可不知也。一则以喜，一则以惧。”（后世多作“一则以忧”）

usage.en: A quotation from the classics; formal, used to support an argument or give advice.
usage.zh: 经典引文，书面语，常用来论证或劝勉。

pinyin: yǐ zhí bào yuàn, yǐ dé bào dé
literal: with · justice · repay · grievance, with · kindness · repay · kindness
natural: Repay a grievance with fairness, and repay kindness with kindness

meaning.en: Treat injury justly rather than with spite, and return kindness in full.
meaning.zh: 对怨恨以公正态度回应，对恩惠以恩惠回报。

equivalents: be just to your enemies and kind to your benefactors

examples.zh: 他被同事误会后没有记恨，而是“以直报怨，以德报德”。
examples.en: After a misunderstanding with a colleague he held no grudge but repaid it with fairness.

examples.zh: 孔子主张“以直报怨，以德报德”，而非无原则的宽容。
examples.en: Confucius advocated this rather than unprincipled forgiveness.

story.en: When someone asked 'What of repaying injury with kindness?', Confucius replied: 'Then what do you repay kindness with? Repay injury with justice, and kindness with kindness.'
story.zh: 有人问“以德报怨，何如？”孔子答：“何以报德？以直报怨，以德报德。”

usage.en: A quotation from the classics; formal, used to support an argument or give advice.
usage.zh: 经典引文，书面语，常用来论证或劝勉。

pinyin: dà yǒng ruò qiè, dà zhì ruò yú
literal: great · courage · seems · timid, great · wisdom · seems · foolish
natural: The truly brave seem timid, and the truly wise seem foolish

meaning.en: Genuinely capable people do not show off and may appear modest or even dull.
meaning.zh: 真正勇敢的人看上去怯懦，真正智慧的人看上去愚笨，不炫耀才能。

equivalents: the wise man hides his wisdom

examples.zh: 他平时不爱说话，却“大勇若怯，大智若愚”，关键时刻总能拿主意。
examples.en: He rarely speaks but is wise beyond appearances and always decides well at crucial moments.

examples.zh: 老教授“大勇若怯，大智若愚”，从不夸耀自己的成就。
examples.en: The old professor never boasts of his achievements.

origin.source: 苏轼《贺欧阳少师致仕启》

story.en: Su Shi's congratulatory letter to Ouyang Xiu on his retirement reads 大勇若怯，大智如愚; the form with 若愚 became the standard. (Compare Laozi: 大巧若拙.)
story.zh: 苏轼《贺欧阳少师致仕启》原作“大勇若怯，大智如愚”；后世常作“若愚”。（参《老子》“大巧若拙”）

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

text: 好学近乎知，力行近乎仁，知耻近乎勇
pinyin: hào xué jìn hū zhì, lì xíng jìn hū rén, zhī chǐ jìn hū yǒng
literal: love · learning · near · wisdom, strive · to act · near · humaneness, know · shame · near · courage
natural: Love of learning is close to wisdom, earnest practice is close to humaneness, and a sense of shame is close to courage

meaning.en: Three roads to the three virtues: study, practice and a sense of shame.
meaning.zh: 爱学习接近智慧，努力实践接近仁爱，知道羞耻接近勇敢。

equivalents: learning, doing and a sense of shame lead to virtue

examples.zh: 校长把“好学近乎知，力行近乎仁，知耻近乎勇”刻在校门口的石碑上。
examples.en: The principal had this line engraved on the stone at the school gate.

examples.zh: “好学近乎知，力行近乎仁，知耻近乎勇”，他以此教导学生。
examples.en: He teaches students with this line.

story.en: In the Doctrine of the Mean, Confucius answers how to get the three virtues of wisdom, humaneness and courage: by love of learning, earnest practice and a sense of shame.
story.zh: 《礼记·中庸》：孔子论智、仁、勇三达德，指出好学、力行、知耻是通往三德的途径。

usage.en: A quotation from the classics; formal, used to support an argument or give advice.
usage.zh: 经典引文，书面语，常用来论证或劝勉。

pinyin: xiǎo shí liǎo liǎo, dà wèi bì jiā
literal: small · time · bright · bright, grown · not · necessarily · fine
natural: One who is clever as a child will not necessarily turn out well as an adult

meaning.en: Early brilliance does not guarantee later achievement; also a witty retort.
meaning.zh: 小时候聪明伶俐的人，长大后未必有出息。

equivalents: a precocious child may not shine later

examples.zh: 神童长大后默默无闻，真是“小时了了，大未必佳”。
examples.en: The child prodigy grew up unknown: this line exactly.

examples.zh: 别太早给孩子贴标签，“小时了了，大未必佳”。
examples.en: Don't label a child too early; early cleverness does not ensure later success.

story.en: The ten-year-old Kong Rong visited the official Li Ying. Chen Wei sneered 'a child who is clever need not turn out well'; Kong Rong retorted 'then you must have been clever as a child' and silenced him.
story.zh: 十岁的孔融拜访李膺，陈韪说：“小时了了，大未必佳。”孔融反唇相讥：“想君小时，必当了了。”

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

pinyin: xié tiān zǐ yǐ lìng zhū hóu
literal: hold · Son of Heaven · to · command · lords
natural: Hold the emperor in one's hands in order to command the feudal lords

meaning.en: Use a figurehead's authority to command others.
meaning.zh: 控制君主，借他的名义发号施令；比喻凭借权威操控他人。

equivalents: use a figurehead's name to command

examples.zh: 曹操“挟天子以令诸侯”，逐步统一了北方。
examples.en: Cao Cao used the emperor's name to command the lords and gradually unified the north.

examples.zh: 这家母公司“挟天子以令诸侯”，借子公司的名义操纵市场。
examples.en: The parent firm manipulated the market under its subsidiary's name.

story.en: In the Longzhong Plan, Zhuge Liang tells Liu Bei that Cao Cao 'holds the Son of Heaven to command the lords' and cannot be opposed head-on; the idea also appears in earlier texts such as the Zhanguo Ce (挟天子以令天下).
story.zh: 《隆中对》中诸葛亮说曹操“挟天子而令诸侯”，不可与之争锋；类似说法亦见于《战国策》（挟天子以令天下）。

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

text: 机关算尽太聪明，反算了卿卿性命
pinyin: jī guān suàn jìn tài cōng míng, fǎn suàn le qīng qīng xìng mìng
literal: schemes · calculate · exhaust · too · clever, instead · calculate · dear · dear · life
natural: Having schemed to the limit and being far too clever, she ends up calculating away her own life

meaning.en: Excessive scheming can backfire and destroy the schemer; originally about Wang Xifeng.
meaning.zh: 过分算计，反而害了自己性命；原指《红楼梦》中的王熙凤。

examples.zh: 他到处耍心眼，结果“机关算尽太聪明，反算了卿卿性命”。
examples.en: He played tricks everywhere and in the end was too clever by half.

examples.zh: 评论家用“机关算尽太聪明，反算了卿卿性命”来评价王熙凤的命运。
examples.en: Critics use this line to comment on Wang Xifeng's fate.

story.en: From the song 'Burdened by Cleverness' (《聪明累》) in the Dream of the Red Chamber, ch. 5, the fate-song for Wang Xifeng, the scheming manager of the Jia household.
story.zh: 出自《红楼梦》第五回《红楼梦曲》中的《聪明累》，为王熙凤的判曲。

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

pinyin: gēng dāng wèn nú, zhī dāng fǎng bì
literal: plough · should · ask · servant, weave · should · consult · maid
natural: Ask the farmhand about ploughing and consult the maid about weaving

meaning.en: Consult the specialists who do the work.
meaning.zh: 耕田要请教种田的仆人，织布要请教织布的婢女，比喻办事要向内行人请教。

equivalents: consult the people who know the job

examples.zh: 项目遇到技术问题，不妨“耕当问奴，织当访婢”，向一线工人请教。
examples.en: When a project hits a technical problem, ask the front-line workers.

examples.zh: 老板说：“耕当问奴，织当访婢”，别光听专家的。
examples.en: The boss said to consult the specialists on the floor, not only the experts.

story.en: The general Shen Qingzhi, advising Emperor Wen of Liu Song against a northern campaign planned by scholars, said 'govern the state as you would a household: ask the farmhand about ploughing and the maid about weaving'.
story.zh: 名将沈庆之劝宋文帝勿听文人北伐之议，说：“治国譬如治家，耕当问奴，织当访婢。”

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

pinyin: dào zhī suǒ cún, shī zhī suǒ cún
literal: the Way · of · where · lies, teacher · of · where · lies
natural: Where the Way resides, there the teacher resides

meaning.en: Whoever has knowledge and truth can be one's teacher regardless of age or status.
meaning.zh: 道理存在的地方，就是老师所在的地方；不论年龄和地位，谁懂得道理谁就是老师。

examples.zh: 向年轻同事请教电脑技术，也是“道之所存，师之所存”。
examples.en: Asking a young colleague about computers is also this: learn from whoever knows.

examples.zh: 《师说》的核心观点就是“道之所存，师之所存”。
examples.en: The core idea of 'On Teachers' is this line.

story.en: Han Yu, in 'On Teachers', argues that regardless of high or low rank or age, the one who has the Way is the teacher.
story.zh: 韩愈《师说》：“是故无贵无贱，无长无少，道之所存，师之所存也。”

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

pinyin: bì qí ruì qì, jī qí duò guī
literal: avoid · their · sharp · spirit, strike · their · slack · return
natural: Avoid the enemy at his keenest, and strike when his spirit flags and he is returning home

meaning.en: Wait until the enemy is weary or demoralised before attacking.
meaning.zh: 避开敌人锐气正盛之时，等其士气衰竭、懈怠思归时再攻击。

equivalents: bide your time until the enemy tires

examples.zh: 球队开场先防守，打算“避其锐气，击其惰归”，下半场再反击。
examples.en: The team defended at the start, planning to wait for the other side to tire and counterattack in the second half.

examples.zh: 谈判时他采取“避其锐气，击其惰归”的策略。
examples.en: In negotiations he followed a strategy of avoiding the keen edge first.

story.en: In the Junzheng chapter, Sunzi lists ways to manage morale: 'in the morning the spirit is keen, by day it flags, by evening it turns homeward; so a good commander avoids its keenness and strikes when it is slack'.
story.zh: 《孙子·军争》论治气：“朝气锐，昼气惰，暮气归，故善用兵者，避其锐气，击其惰归。”

date.zh: 春秋末至战国 · 前5世纪
date.en: late Spring and Autumn to Warring States, 5th c. BC

usage.en: A quotation from the classics; formal, used to support an argument or give advice.
usage.zh: 经典引文，书面语，常用来论证或劝勉。

pinyin: mǐ bù yǒu chū, xiǎn kè yǒu zhōng
literal: none · not · have · beginning, few · can · have · end
natural: Everything has a beginning, but few are able to see it through to the end

meaning.en: Many start well but few finish; a warning to persevere.
meaning.zh: 凡事都有开端，但很少有人能坚持到底，提醒人要善始善终。

equivalents: well begun is half done, but finishing is harder

examples.zh: 健身房的会员，往往“靡不有初，鲜克有终”。
examples.en: Gym members often start strong but few see it through.

examples.zh: 创业之初要谨记“靡不有初，鲜克有终”。
examples.en: At the start of a business, bear this line in mind.

story.en: From the ode 'Dang' in the Book of Songs, in which King Wen of Zhou laments the decline of Shang: 'Heaven gave birth to the people, but its decrees are not to be relied on; all have a beginning, few an end.'
story.zh: 《诗经·大雅·荡》：文王叹商纣失道，言“天生烝民，其命匪谌。靡不有初，鲜克有终”。

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: A quotation from the classics; formal, used to support an argument or give advice.
usage.zh: 经典引文，书面语，常用来论证或劝勉。

pinyin: huáng zhōng huǐ qì, wǎ fǔ léi míng
literal: yellow · bell · smashed · discarded, clay · pot · thunder · sounds
natural: The great bronze bell is smashed and discarded while clay pots thunder

meaning.en: Worthy people are cast aside while worthless ones are celebrated; a protest against a topsy-turvy world.
meaning.zh: 贤能的人被抛弃，庸才却得志喧嚣，指是非颠倒、贤愚不分。

equivalents: the worthy cast aside, the worthless celebrated

examples.zh: 有才华的人被埋没，而平庸者身居高位，真是“黄钟毁弃，瓦釜雷鸣”。
examples.en: Talented people are buried while mediocre ones take high office: this line exactly.

examples.zh: 他在文章里用“黄钟毁弃，瓦釜雷鸣”批评用人不公。
examples.en: In his essay he criticised unfair appointments with this line.

story.en: In the Chu Ci poem 'Divination', Qu Yuan, banished, asks a diviner whether to compromise with the world or keep to his principles, and laments that the age favours the base over the noble.
story.zh: 《楚辞·卜居》：屈原被放逐，问卜于太卜郑詹尹，慨叹世道混浊，贤士无名。

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

pinyin: jiā lěi qiān jīn, zuò bù chuí táng
literal: household · pile · thousand · gold, sit · not · at edge of · hall
natural: A man with a thousand pieces of gold does not sit at the edge of the hall

meaning.en: The rich avoid risk because they have much to lose.
meaning.zh: 家财万贯的人不会坐在屋檐边上，怕瓦掉下来砸到自己；比喻富贵之人爱惜自身，不涉险境。

equivalents: people with much to lose avoid risks

examples.zh: 他当了老板就不再亲自冲锋陷阵，所谓“家累千金，坐不垂堂”。
examples.en: Since becoming boss he no longer leads the charge himself: this line.

examples.zh: “家累千金，坐不垂堂”，有钱人更注重安全。
examples.en: The rich are more careful about safety.

story.en: Sima Xiangru, trying to dissuade Emperor Wu of Han from dangerous hunting trips, quotes the proverb 'a family with a thousand gold does not sit under the eaves'; the shorter form 千金之子，坐不垂堂 appears in the biography of Yuan Ang.
story.zh: 司马相如上书谏汉武帝勿涉险打猎，引谚“家累千金，坐不垂堂”；《袁盎晁错列传》则作“千金之子，坐不垂堂”。

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

pinyin: cóng shàn rú dēng, cóng è rú bēng
literal: follow · good · like · climbing, follow · evil · like · collapse
natural: Following good is like climbing up, following evil is like a landslide

meaning.en: Doing good takes effort, but sliding into bad habits is quick and easy.
meaning.zh: 学好像登山一样艰难，学坏却像山崩一样迅速。

equivalents: it's uphill to do good and downhill to do wrong

examples.zh: 沉迷游戏的坏习惯一旦染上，就应了“从善如登，从恶如崩”。
examples.en: Once a bad habit like gaming is picked up, this line comes true.

examples.zh: 教育孩子要明白“从善如登，从恶如崩”的道理。
examples.en: In educating children one must understand that virtue is hard won and vice easily caught.

story.en: From the Guoyu (Discourses of the States), in the Zhou section: a court speaker cites this proverb to warn that goodness is hard to attain but vice is quickly caught.
story.zh: 出自《国语·周语下》，引谚语说明学好难、学坏易。

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。
